changes: 🔍 The Video tab was throwing away most of a screen share before drawing it. Every stream was squeezed to 960 pixels across and re-encoded — fine for a camera tile the size of a stamp, ruinous for a 3440-wide desktop full of code. Shares now keep 1920 across at a much higher quality; camera tiles stay cheap (switchb)

🖥️ Screen shares are readable now. The app told LiveKit every share was 1920×1080 no matter what the monitor really was, and LiveKit plans the encoder from that number — so anyone on a bigger screen was being encoded as if it were 1080p, at a bitrate meant for a desktop in motion rather than a page of code (switchb)

It now reports the real screen (aimed at 1440p on a 4K one, so encoding stays within a normal machine's means) and asks for far more bitrate at 15fps. A shared editor is nearly a still image; sharp text is worth more than smooth motion, and if the connection can't keep up it now costs frames rather than sharpness

🎵 Queued songs show their real names. A SoundCloud playlist doesn't tell us any titles up front, so the queue filled with names invented from the link — and for some playlists the link is a bare id, which is why most of the queue read as a row of digits (switchb). The bot now looks the names up in the background while the first song plays

🔀 Shuffle the music queue (switchb). There's a Shuffle button next to Clear in the queue rail, one in the phone's Up next list, and `shuffle` works as a command. It reorders what's waiting — whatever is playing keeps playing

👤 Avatars on the phone, and messages group the way they do on the desktop. Four messages in a row from one person used to repeat their name and the time four times; now it's one avatar, one name, and the rest of the run underneath it (switchb)
🌈 Names are coloured on the phone, same as the desktop — your role's colour if you have one, otherwise the colour your avatar already uses (switchb)

🧩 Stickers on the phone. You could always SEE them (a sticker is just an image), but there was no way to send one — there's a sticker button in the composer now, and a sticker on its own renders sticker-sized instead of filling the screen

🔄 The web app notices when a new version has been deployed and reloads itself. Installed to a home screen it used to run whatever it first booted with, which is why a feature could ship and your phone would carry on without it

📁 The phone groups channels the way the desktop does. Categories were shipped a while back and the web app was ignoring them entirely — tap a group to fold it, and which ones you keep shut is remembered on that phone. A folded group still shows anything unread
⌨️ Typing indicators on the phone, both ways: it shows who's typing and tells everyone else when you are
📌 Pinned messages are marked, the drawer shows the server's actual name (and notices when it's renamed), and errors from the server now appear instead of vanishing

📱 Server emojis finally show up in the web app. Until now a message using one arrived on your phone as the literal text ":blobwave:" — the phone had no idea the server had emojis at all. They render, and the list updates when someone adds one
Ordinary text with colons in it is left alone, as before: a link, a time like 12:30, and an emoji name nobody has made all stay exactly as typed

😀 Emoji autocomplete in the composer (Jon's #6). Type `:fi` and it offers 🔥 and any server emoji whose name starts that way — server ones first. ↑↓ to choose, Enter or Tab to take it, Escape to dismiss just that word

🙂 Typed faces get offered too — `:)` `:D` `:O` `:P` `;)` and friends. These only ever suggest: Enter still sends your message exactly as you typed it, and only Tab swaps in the emoji, because ":)" is a message plenty of people mean to send as-is (switchb)

🖼️ Opening an image no longer traps you on it (Jon's #4). Arrows either side step through the channel's photos, ← and → do the same, and it says where you are — "3 of 12". Open one from the Files panel and it walks that list instead
📱 The web app gets a proper viewer too, where it had none: photos opened in a new tab before. Swipe left or right to move between them, tap outside to close

🤫 The bot stops announcing what it queued. Adding a song posted a line in whatever channel you typed the command in — which is how it ended up talking in #feature-requests — and the queue in the rail already shows the same thing, better
It still speaks up when something goes wrong, and when a Spotify playlist is too long to take whole, since the queue can't tell you that part

🚪 Logging out no longer forgets the server. It stays in the rail, greyed out, with your username already filled in — sign back in with just the password. Until now "Log out" quietly deleted the whole entry, which is how switchb's second server vanished
To actually drop a server, click its greyed tile and choose "forget this server" on the login screen

🗂️ Channel categories. Admins can group the channel list in Server settings → Channels; everyone can fold a group shut, and which ones you keep open is remembered on your machine. Channels you haven't filed stay at the top, so nothing moves until someone makes a category
📊 A Stats page for admins: people, messages, channels, files, database size and uptime, with the upload cap as a bar. Everything you'd otherwise have to log into the server to find out

🔊 The volume slider works on the phone. It was setting the audio element's volume, which Chrome on Android ignores outright — the slider moved and nothing happened. Audio now runs through a gain control that every browser honours (switchb)
That also un-sticks the top half of the slider everywhere: an audio element caps at 100%, so anything above it did nothing. 200% is genuinely twice as loud now
🎚️ And the bot plays a bit louder to begin with — it was mixing itself down to 35% so it wouldn't drown out talking, which was more than it needed
🎚️ The volume bar runs the length of the song bar above it and finishes in the same place, starting right after the transport buttons. The "just you" label is gone (JunkfoodJon, switchb)

⏭️ Skipping loads the next song immediately. The look-ahead used to wait until near the end of a track, so a skip arrived before it had started and the next song was fetched from scratch — it now fetches straight away, and re-resolves if the link has gone stale (JunkfoodJon)

🎯 Fixed a song arriving as 121 minutes. When the real upload is DRM protected (SoundCloud's copies of label releases usually are), the bot used to fall through to whatever else the search returned — in switchb's case a two-hour guest mix, which then held the queue. It now only plays a hit whose title actually matches the song and whose length is in the right ballpark, and skips rather than playing something else entirely

🔊 The volume slider in the Music tab is a normal size again. It had been set to fill whatever space was left, so on a wide window it ran the width of the player — it's the same 116px as the one on the chat player now, over on the right of the transport row (JunkfoodJon)

⏭️ Songs run into each other now. The bot used to finish a track and only then go looking for the next one — a search and a download check, about five seconds of silence between every Spotify track. It now gets the next one ready while the current one plays. Measured: 4.9 seconds of dead air, gone

🔇 Mute a channel. Right-click it (or a DM in the rail) and pick Mute: no sound, no toast, no phone notification, even for an @you. The channel dims and its badge goes quiet, but messages still arrive and still count as unread — muting is about noise, not about hiding what people said
Handy now that phone notifications work: mute the busy channels instead of turning the lot off

🎧 NotDiscord has a logo. A headset ring around a gradient N with a speech-bubble tail — on the exe, in the taskbar and alt-tab, in the tray, and as the icon when you install the web app to your phone. It replaces the plain white letter that was standing in
🪟 The window's title bar is our own grey now instead of the one Windows picked — it stopped sticking out above the app (JunkfoodJon)
⚙️ The settings gear sits next to log out instead of floating in the middle of the bar (switchb)
The mark is drawn by a script rather than exported once, so tweaking a colour or a curve is an edit and a re-run, not a redraw

📬 Phone notifications actually arrive now. The server was skipping anyone with a live connection — and the desktop app sits in the tray all day, so switchb's phone had been silenced since the feature shipped. Your phone decides for itself now, and stays quiet only when you're looking at the app on that phone

💬 DIRECT MESSAGES tab in the right sidebar, beside MEMBERS (JunkfoodJon's spec): your conversations newest-first with avatar, name and time, opening in the main view. DMs left the channel list, which is the pile-up switchb pointed at a while back

😊 The emoji picker opens right under the message you're reacting to instead of down by the text box — easier to hit, and it no longer matters whether that message was the most recent one (JunkfoodJon)

😄 The react button works again. Clicking it did nothing visible — it was quietly jumping to the message instead of opening the emoji picker — and it had been that way since replies shipped in v0.18.0, 67 releases ago. Thanks JunkfoodJon for reporting it
Replying and reacting also work together now: the picker opens while a reply is staged, instead of one cancelling the other

🎵 Spotify credentials are two boxes now — client ID in one, secret in the other, exactly as Spotify's dashboard shows them. No more joining them with a colon by hand (JunkfoodJon, who called the old way sloppy, correctly)
✅ And they're checked against Spotify the moment you hit Save, so a typo says so right there instead of turning up later as "couldn't read that Spotify link"
😴 Gentler on Spotify's API: a link is resolved once and remembered, so reposting the same track costs nothing, and if they ever do rate us the bot says how long to wait instead of hammering away

🎨 Code blocks are syntax highlighted. Put a language on the fence — ```rust, ```python, ```sql, ```js, ```json, ```bash and friends — and comments, strings, numbers, keywords and types each get their own colour. A fence with no language looks exactly as it always did

🐛 Fixed while adding it: the phone app was collapsing every message onto one line, so anything multi-line — a code block, a list, a paragraph with a line break — arrived as a run-on. Line breaks and indentation are kept now, in both apps

🔑 The login screen stopped asking for an invite code you don't need. Logging in is just username and password now; "I need an account" flips it to the sign-up form, which is the only place the code belongs (switchb)

🏠 A brand-new server sets itself up now. Point the app (or a browser) at one nobody has an account on and it offers to create it: name the server, make your account — which is the admin — and pick the invite code everyone else will need. No SSH, no guessing which account becomes the owner
▶️ Videos in chat no longer start playing by themselves, or loop forever. That was fine when every clip was two seconds long; it isn't when someone posts a real video (switchb)

🖼️ Link cards on the phone. Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud and the rest now show cover art, title and description instead of a bare URL — and where the site has a player, tapping play opens it right in the message. The server fetches all of it, so opening a channel never tells those sites who's reading

📹 Photos and videos uploaded from the phone now play in the desktop app too. The web app posts its uploads as a path rather than a full link, and the desktop app was showing those as plain text — old messages fix themselves once you're on this version (thanks switchb)
✏️ The phone app can edit and delete your own messages now — admins can delete anyone's, same as on desktop. Deleting asks first, because these are thumb-sized buttons

🗑️ Deleting a message now deletes what it was carrying. A photo or video goes with it, unless something else still points at that file — another message, an avatar, a sticker, an emoji. Before this it sat on the server until the retention sweep noticed it weeks later
Fixed while we were in there: custom emojis weren't protected from that sweep, so one could have been deleted out from under the server once it aged past the retention window

🎞️ Videos shared from a phone play inline again. Android hands over a filename with the gallery's own id stuck on the end, which ran past our 64-character limit — and the part being cut off was the ".mp4", so the app offered a download instead of a player. Long names are still shortened, but never at the extension's expense (thanks switchb)
🎧 Spotify links play! Paste a track, album, or playlist link (or a spotify: URI) and the bot queues it — with Spotify's titles, artists, and cover art

The audio still comes from SoundCloud, because Spotify's API won't stream to a bot. The bot matches by song length so it finds the real track and not a sped-up edit — for big-label songs that may be a fan upload, since SoundCloud's own copies are DRM protected
Playlists queue up to 100 tracks, and the bot says so when it stops there
Needs Spotify credentials in Server settings → Bot (any Spotify developer app; ask Jon nicely)

🔑 Server settings → Bot has a Keys section: the OpenRouter key, GIPHY key, SoundCloud cookie, and Spotify credentials are all set from inside the app now, no server access needed. Keys are write-only — once saved, nobody can read them back out
🧠 You can also pick which model the bot thinks with — any model id from OpenRouter, and it takes effect on the next message
📲 The web app has its own Install button in Settings, because your browser only ever offers on its own once (and never again after you uninstall)
🔔 Phone notifications! Install NotDiscord to your Home Screen, open ☰ → Settings, and turn on notifications for that device — messages reach you with the app closed
⚙️ The web app has a Settings sheet now, with a choice of what to be notified about: everything, mentions & DMs (the default), or nothing. DMs always notify their participants
Notifications only fire when you're not already connected — if the app is open, you'd just see the message
🪟 The app remembers your window size, position, and whether it was maximized — no more resizing it after every update
🔑 If your role changes while you're online (someone promotes you to admin), the app now picks that up on its own instead of leaving you with the badge but none of the buttons

🔍 Double-click a tile in the Video tab to blow it up — it takes the whole panel and chat steps aside, so you can actually watch someone's screen share. Double-click again (or hit the ✕) to go back to everyone. Same gesture the pop-out call window has had

🛡️ Flood protection on the server: messages, reactions, edits and uploads each get a generous burst allowance and then a sane rate, so a runaway script or a stolen account can't fill everyone's screen. Normal chatting is unaffected — you'd have to send ten messages in one second to notice
🐛 Fixed: on a brand-new server the first person to register wasn't made admin (the bot account was being counted as the first user), leaving the owner unable to open server settings

⚡ Images load a lot faster: the server now makes a small preview of every uploaded picture, and chat and the Files panel use it instead of pulling the full-size original (a test photo went from 682 KB to 14 KB — 46× less). Clicking still opens the real thing, and older uploads get previews the first time anyone views them. Phones and slow wifi feel this the most
↔️ The channel and member sidebars now grow with the window — fullscreen on a big monitor no longer leaves usernames truncated next to a giant chat column

🖼️ The share picker shows live thumbnails now — an actual picture of each monitor and window, so you can see what you're about to share instead of guessing from a title. It also moved out of the cramped sidebar into a proper centered picker with room for full names

🔔 Ping toasts: when someone @mentions you or DMs you while you're in another channel (or on the Music/Video tab), a little popup slides in bottom-right with who, where, and what. Click it to jump straight to the message, × to dismiss, or ignore it — it fades on its own after six seconds. Toggle in Settings → App
📢 Pick where the bot posts release notes: Server settings → Bot → Release announcements. Send them to #announcements, keep the default (first text channel), or switch them off entirely
📅 Day dividers in chat: a quiet "Today", "Yesterday", or full date line between days, so scrollback stops running together
⤓ "Back to now": scroll up into history — or land there from a search hit or a pin — and a chip floats above the composer to take you back to the newest message in one click

🐛 Fixed: clicking another server in the far-left rail did nothing — you stayed logged into the one you were on. Turns out nobody had ever actually had two servers until today. Switching works now, both directions

🪟 Share a single window! The share button now always opens a picker: your monitors on top, every open window below — share just the game or just the browser instead of your whole screen. If the shared window closes, the share ends itself instead of freezing on the last frame
NotDiscord's own windows aren't offered for sharing (the hall-of-mirrors special is no more)

📱 The phone app grows up: messages render real formatting (bold, lists, code, quotes, links, @mentions), you can react (😊 button for the quick six, tap a pill to join in) and reply (↩ on any message), and unread badges show on channels, people, and the menu button so you know something's waiting
📱 In calls: a deafen button, and a volume slider per person — turn a loud friend down without leaving the couch

Stickers and custom emojis no longer clutter the Files panel — it lists files people actually shared. (And no, sending a sticker never made a new file: the image uploads once when the sticker is created, every send reuses it)

🗂️ The Files panel (Jon's spec): a new button next to the pin swaps the right sidebar for every file ever posted in the channel — image thumbnails, type icons for the rest, with name, who posted it, when, and size. Click to open, right-click to jump to its message, save, or copy the link. Click it again or click back into chat to bring the members back

🧹 Sidebar dedup (the design Jon and switchb picked): voice channels show who's inside as small stacked avatars right on the row — hover for names, LIVE pill if someone's sharing. The name-by-name roster under the channel is gone; the tile at the bottom is the one place with names, sliders, and controls
Direct Messages can fold away — click the header to collapse. DMs with unread messages (and the one you have open) stay visible, so nothing sneaks past you. Your choice sticks between launches

💚 Speaking rings on desktop now work like the phone's (which switchb noticed were more accurate): every ring — including your own — follows the server's reading of the audio actually being transmitted, instead of a local guess. If your ring is lit, people can hear you; if it isn't, they can't. Measured: lights ~0.7s after you start talking, clears ~1.2s after you stop

🎙️ VOICE ON YOUR PHONE. The web app's menu has a Voice section — tap the channel, allow the mic, and you're in the call with everyone on desktop. A bar above the message box shows who's talking, with mute and hang-up. If you deny the mic you still join listening-only
📱 The web app now uses the same icons as the desktop app (Jon's ask) — menu, music, members, send, transport, all of it. One icon set, one app
Phone voice is audio-only for now: no screen share or camera from the browser yet, and no music-bot volume slider — those are next

📱 Web app round two: the 👥 button slides in a members panel (avatars, ADMIN badges, statuses, online dots, and a 🔊 for whoever's in voice), and the 🎵 button opens a Music tab — now playing with art and progress, pause/skip/stop, the queue with remove, and paste-a-link-to-queue. Your phone is now the couch remote for the music bot
Voice on the phone is the next big one — it needs the browser's own WebRTC stack, so it gets its own release

📹 Turning on your camera no longer pops open the separate call window — your preview lives in the Video tab like everything else. The pop-out window still exists for whoever wants it: the Watch buttons in the voice list open it

📱 NotDiscord on your phone: open notdiscord.switchbhost.com/app in your phone's browser, log in, and chat — text, images, DMs, live updates. On Android Chrome hit ⋮ → "Add to Home screen" (iPhone: Share → "Add to Home Screen") and it installs like an app, icon and all
The web app is chat-first for now: voice, video, and music stay on the desktop app while we teach the browser to do WebRTC
🎚️ Auto mic level: quiet laptop mics get boosted toward normal speech volume automatically, like Discord does. On by default; toggle in Settings → Voice if you prefer raw
🎙️ Laptop mic arrays that ship out-of-phase stereo channels no longer cancel themselves to near-silence — we now take the strongest channel instead of averaging

🔊 Fixed for Jon: "audio output failed to open: Cannot change thread mode after it is set". Opening the System-default speaker touches a Windows API that demands a specific COM thread mode, and on some Windows builds it refuses — our audio threads now claim the right mode up front

💬 Custom status: open your profile (click yourself, bottom left) → Set status. It shows under your name in the members list, on your profile, and in your own corner — "away", "gaming", whatever. Empty clears it

⏩ Video seeking works: you can finally scrub shared clips to any point instead of watching from the start. The server now speaks HTTP range requests, which also means a dropped update download can resume instead of starting over

🎙️ Fixed: mic sensitivity could let audio through while nobody looked lit up. The slider, the level bar, and the threshold marker were all on different scales — now they share one dB scale, so the knob sits exactly on the marker and the bar shows the same peaks the gate hears
The level bar now lives directly under the sensitivity slider (it was stranded under Mic volume), so "set the line just below your voice" finally works as written
Opening the gate now takes ~30ms of sustained sound instead of one 10ms spike, so a keyboard click can't broadcast half a second of your room
📧 Add an email to your account (Settings → Account): we send a 6-digit code, you type it back, done. Your email is private — nobody on the server can see it
🔑 Forgot your password? The login screen can now email a reset code to your verified address — no more asking an admin to poke the database
The music tab's queue rail is now exactly as wide as the members list, so swapping Chat ↔ Music doesn't shift the middle panel around (Jon's ask)
Server settings moved off the channel title and onto the server name at the top left, where they belong (also Jon's ask). The channel title is just a title again

📌 Pinned messages: admins can right-click any message to pin it (in DMs, both of you can). Pinned messages get a little gold pushpin, and the pushpin button next to the channel name lists a channel's pins — click one to jump straight to it
Jumping to a message (a pin, a reply's original) now actually scrolls it into view instead of highlighting it somewhere off-screen
📹 Fixed: video tiles only refreshed when you switched tabs, and showed a broken-image icon until they did. They now update continuously on their own
The "+ new channel" box is gone from the bottom of the channel list — channels are made in Server settings → Channels now, and the list fills the space it left

🖥️ Fixed: when you shared your screen, everyone could see it except you — your own tile just showed your avatar. You now get a tile of your own share like everybody else, in the call window and the Video tab
🐛 Fixed: you could only ever have ONE direct message on the whole server. Every DM after the first silently failed — clicking Message on someone's profile did nothing. DMs now work with everyone

📹 There's a Video tab next to Chat and Music (Jon's spec): everyone in the call gets a tile in the middle panel — screen shares and cameras live, everyone else as their avatar — with mute, deafen, camera, share and leave underneath, and chat still below it
Pasting a link on the Music tab no longer posts the command and a big preview card to the channel. It just queues, and the bot's one line is all you see

🎛️ Click the channel name at the top to open server settings: channels (rename, delete, create), the server's name/icon/invite, roles and members, the bot, and storage — all in one panel instead of a small modal

The Permissions page spells out exactly what an admin can do and what a member can do. There are still only those two roles — per-channel permissions aren't built yet, and the page says so rather than showing switches that do nothing
Channels can be renamed now (admins), and the new name reaches everyone straight away
🎵 The music queue moved to the right-hand panel, so the chat gets its height back — the player and its controls stay where they were

🔊 The music itself sounds better: it's published at 128kbps stereo instead of the 48kbps speech setting it was using, with the noise-gating that chopped quiet intros switched off, and it now pulls the artist's original file from SoundCloud where one is offered
The gear menu keeps your own settings (voice, app, account); server-wide settings live in the new panel

🖱️ Right-click actually does something now, and only when there's something to do: a message offers Reply / Add reaction / Copy text / Edit / Delete, an image offers Save image as, a person offers Message / Mention / admin actions, a queue track offers Play next / Remove, and any text box offers Cut / Copy / Paste / Select all
The old browser menu (Back, Reload, Print, Save as…) is gone — none of it did anything useful here. Right-clicking empty space now opens nothing at all instead of a menu of junk
Numbered lists keep their numbers: typing 1. 2. 3. used to turn them into bullets and throw the numbers away. A list that starts at 7 starts at 7
The message box stays in the same place when you switch between Chat and Music — no more jumping, and the empty strip underneath it is gone
Fixed the music queue drawing on top of the chat underneath it
Icons instead of bare text on the queue's tick boxes, Remove selected, Clear, the up/down arrows and the "just you" volume tag
The message box spell-checks what you type (the search box doesn't, so names and slang stay unmarked)
🖥️ Double-click someone's screen share or camera in the call window and it fills the whole window — double-click it again to get everyone back
There's a Fullscreen button up in the corner of the call window (F11 works too), so a stream can have your entire monitor instead of sharing it with an avatar
Escape backs out one step at a time — the big stream first, then fullscreen. It never hangs up on you

🎵 The music tab is here (Jon's design): Chat / Music tabs at the top right of the channel — the Music tab is a real player with cover art, a progress bar, play/pause/skip/stop, and your own volume slider
The queue is shared and editable: reorder with ▲▼, tick tracks and remove several at once, or clear the lot — everyone sees the same queue within a second
On the Music tab, pasting a link and hitting enter just queues it — no command to remember
Chat stays right underneath so the room keeps talking while the music plays
Fixed a nasty one: the voice channel list could empty itself if the server briefly couldn't reach the voice service
The call window now shows everyone in the call, not just whoever's sharing video — people on audio get their avatar, so it looks like a group call
Someone's video appears in their tile the moment they turn a camera or share on; no need to hit Watch again
Your own camera is a tile alongside everyone else's now, instead of a thumbnail in the corner
Video is a real call window now: everyone's stream side by side with their name on it, your own camera in the corner, and a call timer up top
Mute, deafen, camera, share screen and leave are right there in the window — no more hunting for the app
Whoever's talking gets a green border, like the speaking ring in the app
Watch a screen share and a camera at once; closing the window stops watching but keeps you in the call
Turning on your camera now opens a preview of yourself, so you can see what everyone else sees (it closes when you turn the camera off)
The voice channel list is now kept honest by the server checking who's really in the call — no more ghosts or invisible people, whatever your client is doing
Fixed disappearing from the voice channel list while still in the call — a brief connection blip used to make you invisible to everyone until you rejoined
Custom emojis! Upload one from the emoji picker (+ button) and use it anywhere as :name: — in messages and as reactions
An emoji-only message renders them big
Fixed Watch doing nothing after you'd already watched something once — you can now watch a screen share and a camera at the same time, in separate windows
The tray Quit actually quits now (third time's the charm), and Settings → App has a Quit button that always works
Unread counts! Channels show how many messages you've missed — red when something pings you
A NEW line marks exactly where you left off when you open a channel
Read state lives on the server, so it survives restarts and stays in sync across your devices
The music bot is no longer deafening — it's mixed well below voice, so the volume slider finally has room in both directions
Slash commands! Type / in the message box and pick from the menu — no more memorizing bot syntax
The music bot now posts a player card with real ⏯ ⏭ ⏹ buttons — click to pause, skip, or stop
One card that updates itself instead of a wall of 'now playing' lines, and it lists what's up next
Settings → Voice has a Test button: hear exactly which device NotDiscord plays to (join cues included)
🎶 THE MUSIC BOT IS HERE. Join a voice channel and tell the bot: play <soundcloud link> — it joins your channel and DJs for everyone
Playlists queue up whole; skip / queue / stop do what they say
The bot announces each track in chat and leaves when the queue runs dry
The bot can draw! Ask it to draw/generate anything and it posts a real image (~4¢ a picture on the server's OpenRouter key)
The bot can see: post an image and ask about it
The bot can search the web for current stuff — news, charts, versions, scores
Admins can now rename the bot and give it an avatar (Settings → Server)
NotBot's personality is now editable: Settings → Server → NotBot personality (admins). Write anything; Reset restores the default
The default personality is, by unanimous crew decision, an anime waifu (◕‿◕✿)
Meet NotBot 🤖 — @NotBot in any channel and it answers (it knows the chat history and the release notes)
NotBot announces new releases in #general the moment they ship
It remembers: long-term per-channel memory with automatic compaction, so it keeps context instead of starting fresh every question
Songs and videos now play in a floating mini-player above the compose box — chatting no longer kills the music (it used to; sorry)
The mini-player has its own volume slider and a close button, and keeps playing while you switch channels
The tray menu actually works now — Open opens, Quit quits (it never did; left-click was carrying the team)
Fixed 'could not stage update: Access is denied' — a leftover locked file from an earlier update could block every future one
Only one NotDiscord runs at a time: launching a second just brings the existing window up (stray hidden copies were also what broke updates)
Emoji picker for typing messages — the smiley button next to GIF opens a searchable grid of ~440 emoji
Type to filter ("fire", "skull", "moai"...), click to drop it into your message; the panel stays open for combos
Invite code management: admins can see, copy, change, or shuffle the signup code in Settings → Server — no more SSHing into the box
Fixed the SoundCloud/YouTube player showing a black box (the browser engine was lazily never-loading it — same fix for grey-cloud preview images)
Voice join/leave blips now play through your chosen voice output device instead of the Windows default — and you hear your own joins and leaves too
The DM call ring moved to your voice output device as well
Link previews! Post a link and you get a card with the title, blurb, and artwork
SoundCloud, YouTube, Spotify and Vimeo links get a play button — the track plays right in the chat window
The server fetches previews, not your client, so linking somewhere never hands that site your IP
Server storage cap (default 30 GB) — admins see usage with a meter in Settings → Server and can raise or lower the cap
Uploads are politely refused when the server is full instead of eating the disk
NotDiscord is now self-hostable: a Docker kit in the repo spins up a full server (chat + voice + HTTPS) in minutes
Pick which monitor to share — multi-monitor setups get a chooser when you hit the share button (single-monitor folks share instantly like before)
Fixed the crash when clicking Watch on someone's screen share (the viewer window was colliding with the main window's internals)
Crashes now leave a crash.log next to your settings so we can actually diagnose them
You can finally change your password: Settings → Account (it logs out your other devices too)
New passwords have real strength rules now — length, variety, and no top-40 classics like 'password1'
Signup enforces the same rules, so no more hilariously weak passwords
Video calls! Hit the camera button in the voice panel to turn on your webcam
People with cameras on get a green CAM pill — click Watch to open their video
Works everywhere voice does: channels and private DM calls alike
Screen share! Hit the monitor button in the voice panel to go LIVE with your primary screen
Sharers get a red LIVE pill next to their name — everyone in the channel gets a Watch button
Watching opens a resizable viewer window; close it whenever you're done
Fixed badge overflow in the members list (long tags now truncate)
The window can no longer be shrunk into oblivion (900x560 minimum)
Private calls! Open a DM and hit the phone button — your friend gets a ring and a Join/Ignore card
Calls are fully private: the rest of the server can't even see one is happening
DMs with a live call show a green phone in the sidebar
Mic sensitivity slider — voice activity now only transmits when you speak above the threshold (marker shown on the mic meter; 0 = classic open mic)
Join/leave blips when people enter or exit your voice channel (toggle in settings)
Replies! Hover a message → reply; click the reference line on any reply to jump to the original
@ mention autocomplete — type @ and pick with arrows + Enter/Tab
Destructive actions now ask for confirmation: deleting channels, bans, admin changes, tag/sticker deletion
Voice channels can now be deleted too (admins, with confirmation)
Message search! The box in the top-right searches all history — click a result to jump to it
Your DMs are only searchable by you
Fixed the tray menu; requests retry automatically on flaky connections
Custom tags! Admins can create colored role tags (any name, any color) and assign them from profile cards
Tags show as pills next to names, and your first tag's color becomes your username color in chat
Create voice channels! Click the # next to the new-channel box to switch it to voice
New notification sound: a proper ba-bloop instead of the Windows ding (for Jon)
Server icons: admins can set one in Settings → Server — shows in the server rail
Uploads now expire to keep the server's disk in check — 3 weeks by default
Admins can pick the retention window in Settings → Server (3 weeks / 1 / 2 / 3 months)
Avatars and stickers never expire
See who's in a voice channel right in the sidebar, without joining (thanks space_goat)
@everyone pings the whole server — use responsibly or get banned by the admin
Server rail: the app can now hold multiple servers — click + on the far left to add one, click circles to switch
Servers have names now — admins can rename theirs in Settings → Server
System tray: closing the window keeps NotDiscord running in the tray
The tray icon gets a red badge when you have unread messages
This screen! After every update you'll see what changed
Browse recent version history any time from Settings → App → What's new
Push-to-talk: pick a key in Settings → Voice — works even while you're in a game
Deafen button in the voice panel (silences everyone + mutes you)
Real settings menu: gear button in the bottom-left
Direct messages! Click someone in the members list → Message
DMs are private end to end — server enforced, admins can't peek
Roles: admin & member, with ADMIN badges — admins can delete messages/channels, promote, and ban
Update downloads stream with a progress bar and no longer stall
RNNoise ML noise suppression (keyboard clatter begone) — toggle in voice settings
Mic volume, output volume, and a live mic meter
Proper SVG icons everywhere instead of emoji buttons
Bare URLs are clickable; right-click copy/paste works
webm/mp4 links play inline like GIFs
Pasted/dropped files show a preview before sending (Enter to send, Esc to cancel)
Per-friend volume sliders and instant speaking rings in voice
The auto-updater itself — this is why you never reinstall manually anymore
Custom stickers: upload once, spam forever
Nightly server backups
